links.outcome: Numerical accuracy of LLM-generated propofol PK code versus reference, including unit and time-scale errors
links.effect: 195/200 runs (97.5%) were Class A (MDAPE <1%). 5 runs (2.5%) were defective: 3 Class C from time-scale/unit errors, 1 empty-CSV failure, 1 duplicated-bolus error. Unit/structural bugs persisted despite prompt method specification.
links.quote: LLMs generate numerically accurate Marsh-model code in most runs but silently diverge in a clinically non-negligible minority.

unlisted_practices: Reference-based numerical validation of LLM-generated pharmacokinetic simulation code before safety-relevant use
Prompt-level specification of numerical method (mandating RK4 integrator and step size) to reduce algorithm-selection errors

screen.practice: prompt-level method specification (mandated integrator) and reference-based validation of LLM-generated code
screen.reason: The study evaluates the safety and accuracy of LLMs generating pharmacokinetic simulation code and explicitly compares unconstrained prompts vs. prompt-level method specification (mandating numerical integrator and step size) to test if it mitigates simulation bugs.
